{{Navbar-Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker}}
'''Transcontinental Gas Pipeline''' is an operating natural gas pipeline in the United States.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2kQxQtr Transcontinental Gas Pipeline,] Wikipedia, accessed January 2018</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from the Gulf coast of Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Alabama, through Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina, Virginia, Maryland, and Pennsylvania to deliver gas to the New Jersey and New York City area.<ref name=ftmap>[https://www.fractracker.org/2020/02/national-energy-petrochemical-map/ National Energy and Petrochemical Map ], FracTracker, February 28, 2020</ref>

==Background==
The Transcontinental Gas Pipeline is operated by Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company, LLC (Transco), a subsidiary of Williams Partners L.P.<ref>[http://investor.williams.com/press-release/williams/transco-initiates-private-debt-issuance-0 Transco Initiates Private Debt Issuance] Williams, Jan. 19, 2016</ref>

=== Main Line ===

==== Settlements ====
In a 2002 settlement with the EPA and U.S. Department of Justice, Williams Partners agreed to test the soil and groundwater near some of its compressor stations for contamination. This settlement also included a $1.4 million fine and a cleanup program for polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB).<ref name="epa">[https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/transcontinental-gas-pipe-line-corporation-transco-multimedia-settlement Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Corporation (Transco) Multimedia Settlement], EPA, Feb. 1, 2002</ref> “This settlement resolves Transco’s past illegal disposal practices and commits the company to a comprehensive testing and cleanup program that will protect public health and the environment,” said Sylvia Lowrance, EPA’s Acting Administrator for Enforcement and Compliance Assurance.<ref name="epa" />

==== Connection to Sabine Pass LNG ====
In 2017 the pipeline was extended to connect to the Sabine Pass LNG facility in Cameron Parish, Louisiana.<ref>[http://investor.williams.com/press-release/williams/williams-partners-expands-pipeline-capacity-deliver-natural-gas-chenieres-lng Williams Partners Expands Pipeline Capacity to Deliver Natural Gas to Cheniere’s LNG Export Facility at Sabine Pass], Williams, Feb. 1, 2017</ref> In February 2018 the Federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration ordered a seven-day shutdown for a storage tank at the facility in which supercold natural gas leaked between the tank's inner and outer walls, on Jan. 22, 2017<ref name="TP">[http://www.nola.com/environment/index.ssf/2018/02/sabine_pass_lng_ordered_to_shu.html Sabine Pass LNG ordered to shut down leaking gas storage tanks], The Times-Picayune, Feb. 10, 2018</ref> An investigation of the leak uncovered 11 similar incidents that had occurred between 2008 and 2016.<ref name="TP" /> "This incident is a reminder that the expansion of LNG projects poses a grave threat to our communities and our climate," said Nathan Matthews, a staff attorney for the Sierra Club, which released a copy of the report to the public after discovering it on Friday. "It's a relief that no one was hurt, but allowing the facility to continue to operate until it's clear how widespread these issues are would be extremely reckless."<ref name="TP" />

==== Financing ====
Recent financial support for Transcontinental's operations has involved debt financing via bond issues. In January 2016, a US$1 billion private bond placement was underwritten by Barclays, JP Morgan, RBC, Scotiabank and TD Bank.<ref>[https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/35598/transcontinental-gas-pipe-line-company-transco-additional-facility Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company (Transco) Additional Facility], IJGlobal, accessed Aug. 10, 2020.</ref> This was followed in March 2018 by the refinancing of existing company debt through a US$1 billion bond issue involving JPMorgan Chase, Barclays, Crédit Agricole and Wells Fargo.<ref>[https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/41312/transcontinental-gas-pipe-line-company-refinancing-2018 Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company Refinancing 2018], IJGlobal, accessed Aug. 10, 2020.</ref>
===Rivervale South to Market Expansion Project===
In September 2017 Transco applied to FERC for permission for the Rivervale South to Market project, which would consist of updating 10.35 miles of existing Transco pipeline, adding a 0.61-mile pipeline loop, and upgrades and modifications to existing pipeline facilities, all in New Jersey.<ref name="Kallanish" /> The project would increase capacity by 190 mcfd.<ref name="Kallanish" /> The planned in-service date is November 2019.<ref name="Kallanish" />

There have been no development updates since the project was first proposed in 2017, and it it presumed to be cancelled.<ref name="Kallanish" />
===Southeastern Trail Expansion Project===
The project will add additional bidirectional capacity on the Transco pipeline. It received Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) in-service approval on December 23, 2020. Full completion and service of the pipeline was delayed until March 1, 2021 due to winter conditions. As of April 2021 the project was partially complete.<ref name="eia1021" />

=== Northeast Supply Enhancement Project ===
The Northeast Supply Enhancement (NESE) project, included the enhancement of existing Transco infrastructure (the [[Transcontinental Gas Pipeline]]) in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and New York. The initial application for permits for the project were submitted in June 2017.<ref name=":04">{{Cite web|url=https://www.dec.ny.gov/permits/115980.html|title=Northeast Supply Enhancement (NESE) Project - NYS Dept. of Environmental Conservation|website=www.dec.ny.gov|access-date=2022-07-26}}</ref>

In January 2019, Williams Companies applied for permits to build the Northeast Supply Enhancement (NESE) Pipeline as an extension of the Transco that would add ten miles of pipeline in Lancaster, Pennsylvania and 27 miles in New Jersey and New York.<ref>[https://www.dec.ny.gov/permits/115980.html Northeast Supply Enhancement (NESE) Project], Department of Environmental Conservation, accessed March 2020</ref> The pipeline was proposed to transport gas from Pennsylvania through New Jersey, travel underwater in the Raritan Bay and Lower New York Bay, ending about three miles offshore the Rockaway Peninsula in the Queens Borough of New York City.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web|url=https://www.dec.ny.gov/permits/115980.html|title=Northeast Supply Enhancement (NESE) Project - NYS Dept. of Environmental Conservation|website=www.dec.ny.gov|access-date=2022-07-26}}</ref>

In May 2019 the New York Department of Environmental Conservation rejected the pipeline, stating, "Construction of the NESE pipeline project is projected to result in water quality violations and fails to meet New York State’s rigorous water quality standards."<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2019/05/15/nyregion/williams-pipeline-gas-energy.html?smid=em-share New York Rejects Keystone-Like Pipeline in Fierce Battle Over the State’s Energy Future], New York Times, May 15, 2019</ref><ref name="ftmap" />

Environmentalists warned that the proposed expansion would damage wetlands in New Jersey. The pipeline would require a trench to be dug in the wetlands, a natural infrastructure that provides wildlife habitats, filters storm water and act as a flood buffer, noted Hackensack Riverkeeper Bill Sheeran."<ref name="NJ">[http://www.nj.com/bergen/index.ssf/2017/09/gas_pipeline_changes_concerning_for_environmentali.html Gas pipeline plan in Meadowlands concerns environmentalists], NJ.com, Sep. 17, 2017</ref> "The wetlands are the first line of defense against really bad things that can happen to really good people," Sheeran said. "This is just another corporation trying to chip away at the environmental quality of the Meadowlands."

Ahead of the May 17, 2020 deadline for the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation to rule on a key permit for the pipeline expansion project, more than 100 protesters participated in a virtual rally against the proposed expansion which would cut through northern New Jersey and then out approximately 23 miles into New York Harbor to connect with the city's existing gas system. New York City Comptroller Scott Stringer said: “We can’t pretend we are making progress on combating climate change if we continue to build out fracked gas infrastructure that will lock in emissions for years to come.” National Grid has been criticised by groups such as the Environmental Defense Fund and NY Renews, an environmental justice coalition of more than 200 groups across New York State, for failing to analyse the emissions impacts of various gas supply scenarios which the company has published since its original pipeline proposal was rejected by the New York Department of Environmental Conservation in May 2019.<ref>[https://grist.org/energy/does-new-york-need-the-williams-pipeline-its-about-to-decide/ Does New York need a new natural gas pipeline? It’s about to decide.], Grist, May 11, 2020</ref>

In July 2020, Forbes reported that the NESE expansion had been cancelled in light of the developer's failure to obtain the necessary water permit.<ref name="canc">Scott Carpenter, [https://www.forbes.com/sites/scottcarpenter/2020/07/06/oil-and-gas-pipelines-increasingly-losing-legal-challenges/#65a999261e88 Oil And Gas Pipelines Increasingly Losing Legal Challenges], Forbes, July 6, 2020</ref>

In March 2021, Transco requested a two-year extension of the time to construct and place the pipeline into service.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web|url=https://centraljersey.com/2021/03/26/nese-pipeline-granted-two-year-extension/|title=https://centraljersey.com/2021/03/26/nese-pipeline-granted-two-year-extension/|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2022-07-25}}</ref> According to EIA, as of May 2021, the status of the project os 'Announced' and expected to begin service in 2023<ref name="eia" />

The project had encountered heated opposition from activists due to the expected costs and ultimate impacts on climate change, human health.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.stopthewilliamspipeline.org/|title=https://www.stopthewilliamspipeline.org/|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2022-07-25}}</ref>

In May 2024, after multiple rejected permits, Williams abandoned the expansion project.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://citylimits.org/2024/05/14/williams-pipeline-saga-ends-but-the-fight-to-phase-out-gas-continues/|title=https://citylimits.org/2024/05/14/williams-pipeline-saga-ends-but-the-fight-to-phase-out-gas-continues/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Diamond East Expansion Project===
The expansion would have added 1 billion cubic feet of gas transport capacity per day through Pennsylvania and New York. There have been no development updates since 2014 and the expansion project is presumed to be cancelled.<ref name="eia" /><ref name="ftmap" />

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, as of April 2021 the project was officially on-hold, and as of July 2025 it was cancelled.<ref name="eiaapr21" />

===Gateway Expansion Project===
In November 2017, Transco applied to FERC for permission to proceed with its Gateway Expansion Project, which includes building a new compressor unit at Transco’s existing Compressor Station 303 in Essex County, NJ, a new valve and electric transformer also in Essex County, and equipment upgrades at a metering station in Passaic County, NJ.<ref>[https://marcellusdrilling.com/2017/11/williams-files-ferc-appl-for-transco-gateway-expansion-project/ Williams Files FERC Appl for Transco “Gateway Expansion Project”], Marcellus Drilling News, Nov. 16, 2017</ref>

The expansion project involves the replacement of valves, compressors, and associated equiptment to improve natural gas deliverability. It does not include laying any additional miles of pipeline. According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) construction was completed in November of 2019, but the in-service date remains 2021.<ref name="eia" />

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, construction was completed in November of 2019.<ref name="eianov">[https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php "Natural Gas Data, Pipeline Projects,"] Energy Information Agency, November 16, 2020</ref>
===Sabine Pass Compression Project Expansion Project===
The expansion will add additional compression pressure to increase the natural gas transport capacity to the [[Sabine Pass LNG Terminal]] in Louisiana, USA.<ref name="eia" />
===Hillabee Expansion Project, Phase 1===
The expansion runs through Alabama.<ref name="ftmap" />

=== Hillabee Expansion Project, Phase 2 ===
The expansion adds additional pipeline to the Transcontinental Gas Pipeline in Alabama.<ref name="eia" /> It entered service in May 2020.<ref name="Williams" /><ref name="ftmap" />

===Hillabee Expansion Project, Phase 3===
The expansion will add additional pipeline to the Transcontinental Gas Pipeline in Alabama. It is the continuation of the Hillabee Expansion Project, Phase 2. It has been approved by the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.<ref name="eia" /><ref name="ftmap" />

As of October 2025 the project still appeared to be in active development. Construction had yet to begin but an anticipated start year was noted as 2026–2027 by the EIA.<ref name="eia" />

===Regional Energy Access Project (Phase I and II)===
The expansion project will create three delivery paths from Chapin B, Puddlefield B, and Carverton B reciept points on the Leidy lateral to three delivery points on Mud Run Road (PA, 210 MMcf/d Phase I), Station 210 Delivery Pool (NJ, 640 MMcf/d, Phase I), and Trenton Delivery CPH (NJ, 190 MMcf/d, Phase II). The new delivery paths will run from Pennsylvania to New Jersey.<ref name="eia" />

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, as of April 2021 the project had not yet applied for FERC approval.<ref name="eia" />

By March 2023, it was approved by FERC.<ref name="eia" />

As of mid-2023, the project was on track for completion by 2024.<ref name=":1" />

===Gulf Connector Expansion===
The Gulf Connector Project expands the Transco pipeline’s delivery capacity by 475 million cubic feet per day, providing service to Cheniere Energy’s Corpus Christi liquefaction terminal and Freeport LNG Development, L.P.’s liquefaction project.<ref name="williams" />

The expansion provides additional transmission capacity from Station 65 in Louisiana to deliver points in Wharton and San Patricio Counties, Texas.<ref name="sec">[https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/107263/000010726319000007/wmb_20181231x10k.htm The Williams Companies, Inc. Form 10-K], US SEC Annual Report, accessed Sep. 5, 2021.</ref>
=== Appalachian Connector ===
The Appalachian Connector, also referred to as the Western Marcellus Pipeline<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.virginiaplaces.org/transportation/gaspipelineexpansion.html|title=Natural Gas Pipelines in Virginia: Expanding the Transmission Network After Fracking|website=www.virginiaplaces.org|access-date=2022-01-28}}</ref>, was a proposed extension to the Transco Pipeline that would have added gas supply from fields in the Marcellus basin in order to meet both demand domestically and for LNG exports abroad. The pipeline was proposed in 2017 but disappeared from Williams' investor documents and suggestions thereafter. As of December 2021, it had been over four years since development had occurred on the project, so it is considered cancelled.
=== Texas to Louisiana Energy Pathway ===
This is a proposed expansion on the Transcontinental Gas Pipeline primarily to serve LNG demand on the U.S. Gulf Coast. According to the EIA, the developer has applied to FERC for approval.<ref name="eia1021" />

It was completed in February 2025.<ref name=":4" />

=== Southeast Supply Enhancement Project ===
In late October 2024, Williams Companies submitted an application to FERC for an expansion in Virginia and North Carolina, as part of an expansion throughout the region for the company.<ref name=":3" />

The project description: Project includes 30.6 miles of p/l in Pittsylvania Cty, VA and Rockingham Cty, NC, designated as the Eden Loop, and 24 miles of p/l in Guilford, Forsyth, and Davidson Counties, NC, designated as the Salem Loop. Project provides incremental firm transportation capacity (from Station 165 Zn 5 Pooling Pt and Cherrystone Interconnect with MVP) to remove constraints in Zone 5 and meet growing nat gas-fired power gen, comm, res, and ind demand in mid-Atlantic and Southeast US. Project also includes new compresser units at Sta 165 in Pittsylvania Cty, VA, Sta 155 in Davidson Cty, NC, Sta 150 in Iredell Cty, NC, and replacement of compressor units at St 145 in Cleveland Cty, NC.<ref name="eia1021" />

=== Southeast Energy Connector Project ===
The expansion project includes 1.9 miles of new pipe and an 11,110 HP compressor station in Chilton and Coosa Counties, AL to provide new capacity to serve Unit 5 of the Earnest C. Gaston power plant in Shelby Cty, AL. It was completed in 2025.<ref name=":4" />

=== Power Express Project ===
The Power Express project represents an expansion of 950 million cubic feet per day and is expected to enter service in Q3 2030. The project is aimed at supporting the state's data center market, which is the largest in the world.<ref name=":4" />

=== Alabama Georgia Connector Project ===
This project includes compressor unit modifications along existing Mainline from Marengo County, AL, to Walton County, GA. Facility upgrades will enable Transco to deliver incremental firm transportation from Station 85 to multiple existing delivery locations on the Transco Mainline and Transco's Georgia Extension Lateral. Construction began March 2025.<ref name=":4" />

=== Gillis West ===
Gillis West is designed to provide a new interconnect on the Transco system at Gillis Hub to increase delivery capability from Haynesville Shale and Gillis area supplies to Transco Zone 2, serving both export and Southeast U.S. market growth. Project agreement executed and binding Open Season conducted (June 2024). Construction and in-service targeted for Q4 2025 as part of a cohort of Transco upgrades.<ref name=":4" />

=== Decatur Lateral Project ===
The Project consists of the construction of approximately 15.9 mile 20-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline lateral, an approximately 0.8 mile 20-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline (ADM Spur), and associated metering and appurtenant facilities. The Project will allow REX to provide up to 181,400 dekatherms per day of firm natural gas transportation service to two new delivery points in Macon County, Illinois.<ref name=":4" />
